Formulation:
Predisposing: Personal history of atopic conditions (eczema, past asthma).  
Precipitating: Acute flare/trigger of dermatologic condition over past 4 days.  
Perpetuating: Ongoing pruritus → sleep loss → daytime fatigue and concentration problems.  
Protective: Employment, social housing, proactive help-seeking, no substance misuse.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Sleep disturbance and impaired daytime functioning secondary to severe pruritus
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve restful sleep; regain concentration at work; resume hiking
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce itch intensity; restore sleep continuity; monitor mood impact
- Actions (Patient): Adhere to prescribed topical steroid, emollient, and antihistamine; keep trigger diary; use sleep hygiene techniques (cool bedroom, avoid hot showers at night)
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe stronger topical steroid, emollient, fexofenadine; review in 7–10 days; assess sleep and mood; consider referral to dermatology if inadequate response; screen for anxiety/depressive symptoms during follow-up

Secondary Problem: Occupational stress related to physical symptoms
- Patient Goal(s): Maintain productivity without distraction from itching
- Clinical Goal(s): Support coping strategies in workplace
- Actions (Patient): Implement scheduled breaks for skin care; discuss temporary accommodations with employer if needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide medical certificate if required; offer brief CBT-based strategies or referral to psychologist if stress persists

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Skin care routine, medication use, trigger identification, importance of follow-up
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased itch, spread of rash, sleep disruption, mood changes
- Coping Strategies: Moisturizing, cool compresses, relaxation breathing at bedtime, avoid scratching

Consent, Coordination & Review:

- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Yes
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: None at present
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: Within 1 week or sooner if worsening

No mental-health-specific differentials applicable; dermatologic DDx provided (eczema flare, contact dermatitis, scabies) do not constitute primary mental disorders.
